subject.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt-cache continuity breaks across room events and native Responses

question: Does the refreshed candidate prove that every protected-tool execution path is denied before hooks or side effects while keeping schemas visible for cache stability?
rationale: Moving sender restrictions from schema filtering to a centralized runtime gate changes the effective authorization boundary and requires explicit maintainer acceptance after resolving current-main overlap.

options.title: Refresh and security-review
options.body: Rebase the candidate onto current main, resolve native continuation overlap, and verify the canonical gate across direct, queued, compaction, recovery, Codex, and Copilot paths.

options.title: Narrow to cache-only changes
options.body: Retain current schema filtering and land only non-security-sensitive prompt-mode or continuation repairs, accepting continued sender-dependent tool-prefix churn.

options.title: Reject this boundary
options.body: Close the candidate and design another cache-stability approach that does not keep protected schemas visible to unauthorized turns.
